surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 adjusted EBITDA of roughly $63–66 million; SunCoke reported $76.9 million, a substantial beat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consol. Adj. EBITDA: not published; ~$63–66M implied” and “My estimate: Adj. EBITDA ~$66M.”

surprises.description: The preview treated a narrowing within the $250–265 million annual EBITDA range as the base case. Management now expects full-year EBITDA to modestly exceed the range’s $265 million high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects full-year 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA to modestly exceed the high end of its $250-265 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 narrowed inside $250–265M” was described as the base case, “not another raise.”

surprises.description: Industrial Services EBITDA was expected to be about $25–27 million as terminal activity normalized, but it reached $32.1 million. Terminal handling was 6.4 million tons, above the preview’s cited Q1 level of 5.64 million tons, while the company also benefited from an extra month of Phoenix results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Services Q3 adjusted EBITDA jumped to $32.1 million from $18.2 million, aided by an extra month of Phoenix results and higher terminal handling volumes of 6.4 million tons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial Services Adj. EBITDA — target ~$25–27M”; management had guided volumes back “closer to Q1 levels” (5.64Mt).

surprises.description: The preview described any Algoma recovery as unmodeled optionality; SunCoke instead reached a settlement and says it was made whole. The settlement also supported a higher free cash flow outlook of $180–185 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SunCoke reached a confidential settlement with Algoma Steel over its 2025 claim, confirming it was ‘made whole’”; “The company raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to $180-185 million, reflecting the Algoma settlement impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Algoma. $90.1M impairment taken in Q4 2025 ... enforcement is being pursued. Any recovery is unmodeled optionality.”

surprises.description: Domestic Coke sales volume was estimated at about 840,000 tons, but actual volume was 875,000 tons despite the Haverhill I shutdown. Domestic Coke EBITDA also exceeded the preview’s implied $47–50 million quarterly range, reaching $51.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic Coke Q3 adjusted EBITDA rose to $51.1 million from $44 million a year earlier, despite coke sales volumes falling to 875,000 tons from 951,000 tons due to the Haverhill I shutdown.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Domestic Coke sales volume ~840kt (my est.)”; the preview’s implied quarterly Domestic Coke EBITDA was “$47–50M.”

surprises.description: Management cautioned that the Middletown turbine insurance recovery is excluded from guidance and may not arrive until early 2027. The preview had identified insurance proceeds as a possible support for Domestic Coke results, so the recovery is less certain as a 2026 contributor than that framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insurance recovery for the Middletown turbine failure is excluded from guidance and may slip into early 2027; if received in 2026, results would significantly exceed the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Domestic Coke needed “Middletown's returned turbine (restarted May), insurance recovery proceeds, and the 51–52% coal-to-coke yields to all persist,” and flagged the “one-time vs. operating split.”

surprises.description: The preview put liquidity at about $207 million and the revolver balance at $160.5 million; SunCoke ended Q3 with about $276 million of liquidity and paid down $53.5 million of its revolver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SunCoke ended Q3 with ~$276 million liquidity and 2.34x gross leverage, generated $94.8 million in operating cash flow, [and] paid down $53.5 million of its revolver.”
